quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: When entering an interstate highway, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow down to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Use the entrance ramp to speed up and smoothly merge with the fast traffic on the interstate. Do not stop like you would on other roads.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You need to see clearly from all your windows. Remove all snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors before you drive.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Honk your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out of your car and wave down the next vehicle.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if possible. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of the high-speed traffic.

questions.question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means:

options.text: Drivers in both directions may pass.
Drivers next to the broken line may pass.
Drivers next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line next to your lane means you may pass.

questions.question: From top to bottom, traffic lights show colors in this order:

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming at the next intersection.

questions.question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:

options.text: Be able to drive safely at high speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: What does a yellow left turn arrow mean?

options.text: Get ready to give way to oncoming cars.
The protected left turn is ending soon.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. Prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Watch for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, watch for a second train on any track. Do not drive until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: Which statement is true about alcohol and driving?

options.text: If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.
If you are below the legal alcohol limit, your driving is not affected.
Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol affects your judgment, which you need to drive safely.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your judgment. You need good judgment to react safely to things on the road. Any amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely, even if you are below the legal limit.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
Check for other vehicles in the lane you want to enter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes suddenly or without warning.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and blind spots to make sure no vehicles are in your path. Use your turn signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do when driving near a large commercial vehicle?

options.text: Follow it closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. You should avoid driving beside them for long periods.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on snow or ice?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive the same way you do in normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change your speed and direction gradually. Never use cruise control on snow or ice. Your tires may lose grip, and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When should your wheels not point straight ahead?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a traffic light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: When waiting to turn left, keep your wheels straight. If hit from behind, this prevents you from moving into oncoming traffic. On a hill or slope, turn your wheels so your vehicle will not roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: How should you enter a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make other vehicles move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, make sure no vehicles are in your way. Always check for traffic to the side and behind your vehicle before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does a red arrow pointing right on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You may turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
You cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
You may turn in that direction after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means "stop." You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: When must you show proof of insurance to a police officer?

options.text: Only if you are in a collision.
If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and get a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you are in a collision or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. You must show proof of insurance and your license to an officer after a traffic stop or collision.

questions.question: You want to pass a pedestrian on the road, but an oncoming vehicle is coming. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
Keep driving at the same speed. The oncoming vehicle must stop for you.
Honk your horn to make the pedestrian move over.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time when possible. If you want to pass a pedestrian but an oncoming vehicle is approaching, slow down and let the vehicle pass first. Then pass the pedestrian if it is safe.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror frequently to stay aware of traffic behind you.

questions.question: How do stopping distances and collision severity relate to vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause serious problems. As speed increases, collision impact and injury severity increase. Increase your following distance as your speed increases so you can stop safely if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Right turn on red light is permitted with caution.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a diagonal line through a black symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: You must always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: There is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to fully cross the tracks.
The railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
You are carrying two or more young children in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is not enough room on the other side for your vehicle to fully cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, in either direction. Do not stop on the tracks. Make sure your vehicle completely clears the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: When used on roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles when used on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Steep hill ahead.
Winding road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns you of a steep hill ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Ease up on the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ease up on the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain control. Steer in the direction of the skid to straighten your vehicle.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or other property, you must leave a note attached to it. Include your name, phone number, and address.
